sections.h2: Cedar to the north, mesquite to the south
paras: San Antonio is the seat of Bexar County, and the Balcones Escarpment crosses the north side of the county. North and northwest of downtown, out along Loop 1604, I-10 and US 281, the land rises into Hill Country with limestone, Ashe juniper and live oaks.

South of downtown the country flattens. Mesquite and mixed brush take over open ground, and mesquite resprouts from the base after it is cut. A San Antonio forestry mulching job can look completely different depending on which side of the city the land sits.

sections.h2: Check the San Antonio tree ordinance before clearing
paras: The City of San Antonio has a tree preservation ordinance that covers private property inside the city limits and in the city's extraterritorial jurisdiction, or ETJ. The city's guidance calls for a tree permit or a tree affidavit before clearing vegetation, construction or tree removal begins.

Rules change, so confirm what applies to your parcel with the City of San Antonio Development Services Department before work starts. Selective forestry mulching leaves standing whatever trees your plan keeps, so the clearing can follow an approved plan.

sections.h2: Keeping soil in place over the Edwards Aquifer
paras: A band of north Bexar County sits on the Edwards Aquifer recharge zone, which the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality regulates for development. If your project is development on the recharge zone, confirm the requirements with your engineer before clearing begins.

Forestry mulching leaves soil intact and leaves root balls in the ground. A dozer disturbs soil and raises erosion risk. On thin, rocky ground over the recharge zone, keeping the soil where it is makes sense for the land and for whoever owns it next.

sections.h2: Forestry mulching for San Antonio developers and utility corridors
paras: 9 Arrow works for land developers, commercial real estate, and energy and utility providers. For those clients, forestry mulching opens lot lines, pad sites, and pipeline and powerline corridors.

Our [right of way clearing](right-of-way-clearing) opens corridors that typically run 30 to 120 feet wide, often ahead of grading crews, dozers and excavators. For homes and commercial pads, see [land clearing for a building site](site-prep). The [forestry mulching in Central Texas](forestry-mulching-and-land-clearing) page covers the service in full.

faqs.q: Do I need a tree permit for forestry mulching in San Antonio?
faqs.a: You may need a tree permit or tree affidavit for forestry mulching in San Antonio if the property is inside city limits or the city's ETJ. The City of San Antonio's tree preservation ordinance covers clearing on private property there. Check with the Development Services Department before work starts so the plan matches the rules.

faqs.q: Will mesquite come back after forestry mulching near San Antonio?
faqs.a: Mesquite often comes back after forestry mulching near San Antonio because it resprouts from the base when cut. Plan on follow-up work for mesquite ground. On utility corridors, we offer ongoing right-of-way maintenance with tractor and batwing equipment to manage aggressive regrowth such as mesquite.

faqs.q: Do you come from Spring Branch for San Antonio forestry mulching jobs?
faqs.a: Yes, 9 Arrow Land Service is based in Spring Branch and travels to San Antonio forestry mulching jobs. We are a service-area business, so the crew and machines come to your land. Call (210) 247-8410 with the property location and a short description of the job to get started.

faqs.q: How is forestry mulching in San Antonio estimated?
faqs.a: Forestry mulching in San Antonio is estimated after a discovery call, a site visit, or both. Density, tree size and species, topography, access, maneuverability and soil conditions all change how long a job takes. We show the estimate by the day or by the acre, so you can see how the number was built.
